newsitem.title: USA: Jury seated in Fla Reynolds tobacco suit.
newsitem.headline: Jury seated in Fla Reynolds tobacco suit.

text.p: A six-member jury was sworn in Wednesday to hear a wrongful death lawsuit filed by the sister of a smoker against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co.
The panel of four women and two men, as well as two alternates, were sworn in by Circuit Judge Bernard Nachman after just over two days of jury selection.
Opening statements were set to begin at 1 p.m. EDT.

The panel will hear a lawsuit known as Raulerson vs. R.J. Reynolds, in which Dana Raulerson, the sister of smoker Jean Connor, who died of lung cancer, has accused the tobacco company of selling a deadly product.

The panel includes a mother of two children who tried cigarettes as a teenager and now believes she is allergic to cigarette smoke and a woman who smoked in college and has a mother and brother who quit smoking.

The jury also includes a woman who works as an international marketing analyst and began smoking at age 15, and a man who works as a flight simulator maintenance worker who said he was very interested in the Raulerson case.
The final two jurors are a mother who works at Wal Mart and a man who quit smoking in the 1980s and said he believes nicotine is a drug.

The jury panel was selected from a pool of about 35 after two days of questioning by lawyers for Raulerson and R.J. Reynolds. The prospective jurors were asked questions about their personal lives, about addiction and their beliefs about personal and corporate responsibility.

Reynolds lawyers indicated they would focus on Connor and the choices she made, in line with tobacco company strategy in past trials that smokers make the choice to smoke and therefore are responsible for their illnesses.
The lawsuit alleges that Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, deceived the public with misleading ads. Connor died of lung cancer in 1995 at age 49.
